version_history.subject: [PATCH 0/2] mm: fix swapcache writeout and cluster table publication

series_items.subject: [PATCH 1/2] mm: vmscan: allow writeout of swapcache folios without anon mappings
series_items.patch_summary: This patch allows the writeout of swapcache folios without an anonymous mapping, which was previously rejected by pageout(). The change enables reclaim to write out these folios while their swap entries remain referenced. This fix addresses a problem where unfaulted zswap readahead folios could be dirty and in swapcache without an anonymous mapping.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 2/2] mm/swap: publish cluster tables after reacquiring allocator locks
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a memory pressure scenario where swap_cluster_populate() publishes a table while its locks are dropped, allowing a cached allocator to consume and free the table before the populating allocator resumes. The patch ensures that cluster tables are published after reacquiring allocator locks, preventing stale reclaimers from returning isolated clusters to allocation. It also retains cluster locks through scans and restores locks on allocation failure, ensuring correct behavior in various scenarios.

> On Fri, Nov 6, 2026 at 9:04 AM Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com> wrote:

> > Under memory pressure, swap_cluster_populate() can publish a table
> > while its locks are dropped for a sleeping allocation. A cached

> >                                    charge failure cleanup

> > Keep the count table, cgroup table and zero bitmap private until

> > A stale reclaimer can return the isolated cluster to allocation while
> > its locks are dropped. Abandon installation if the list state changes or
> > a table appears, freeing only private allocations. Restore locks on

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] x86/mce: Restore rate limit on MCE logged message

version_history.subject: [PATCH] x86/mce: Restore rate limit on MCE logged message

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch restores a rate limit on Machine Check Exception (MCE) logged messages, preventing a large number of messages from being printed to the console in a short period of time. The rate limit was inadvertently dropped in a previous commit, leading to potential issues with netcons infrastructure. This patch reinstates the original rate limit.
